newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed up aross the board on Monday with rising domestic A share markets boosting demand on the repo market, traders said.
The most active seven-day contract surged to nine percent from 1.01 percent on January 31. The market was closed for two weeks for the Lunar New Year holiday.
Total turnover surged to 8.67 million lots from 2.69 million on January 31. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.

But the improved sales of the new two-year treasury note on the primary market somehow supported the market and prevented the contracts from falling sharply, they said. The note was being issued from January 22 and will be listed on Tuesday.
The most active three-year bond that matures in October 1999 fell slightly to 103.85 yuan from 103.88 yuan on January 31.
Combined volume of the eight-contract markets fell to 1.33 million lots from 2.11 million on January 31.
Traders said the performance of the two-year bond after listing on Tuesday would decide the near-term trend of the T-bill spot market. - Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
